why: builds an executor around a session someone else opened -- the C API's entry point (`rclc_support_init` opens the session, then `rclc_executor_init` wraps it) and the board/BSP paths. It exists because the C and C++ surfaces are implemented ON this type, and their lifecycle splits session creation from executor creation the way rcl does. rclrs has no counterpart: an rclrs executor never adopts a foreign handle. See `rust:Executor::open*`.
